messages:
maria: Heads up — ~30 large-gang jobs (8xA100 reqs) stuck PENDING in us-west1b for ~18m. Warm pool not draining into them. Lots of small single-gpu pods pinned on those racks.

devon: I see the backlog too. Grafana shows node free-gpu count near zero but cluster gpu utilization only ~60% — smells like fragmentation. :thinking:

maria: here's a describe from one pending pod:
```
Name:           training-job-xyz
Status:         Pending
Reason:         Unschedulable
Events:
  Type    Reason             Age    From               Message
  ----    ------             ----   ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling  18m    default-scheduler  0/128 nodes are available: 24 Insufficient GPUs, 104 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```

leo: Can you paste the node taints? I suspect gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule on a subset (reserved for dedicated workloads).

maria: yup, checking nodes in the affected AZ. sample node:
```
k8s-node-uw1b-042 labels: gpu-type=a100, pool=shared-warm, reserved=true
taints: reserved=true:NoSchedule
```

infra-bot: Autoscaler event: scale-up delayed: provisioning quota hit for us-west1b (requested 8 x A100), queueing for region fallback. (ID: asg/6087)

devon: So warmpool nodes are in a separate pool with a taint, and tiny pods are filling remaining non-reserved nodes. Large-gang needs contiguous GPUs / nodes and can't tolerate the taint. Classic fragmentation + taint reservation.

anya: Short-term mitigation options:
- relax reserved taint on a small subset (if allowed)
- bump warmpool.min to add 4 nodes -> will they be tainted?
- evict tiny noncritical pods (burst worker pool) to free slots

sam: Cost note — spinning up 8 A100 instances for 1h ~ $26/hr * 8 = ~$208/hr. If we evict & consolidate tiny pods we avoid extra nodes. Which tenants are on those tiny pods?

maria: quick audit: burst-workers (non-prod), benching jobs, and a couple of canaries. We can evict burst-workers for 30m.

leo: Proposed immediate playbook:
1) Patch warmpool node template to remove reserved=true taint for next 4 nodes (so they join shared pool)
2) Increase warmpool.min by 4 (trigger new nodes without quota if possible)
3) Run a targeted kubectl drain for burst-workers on 3 nodes to open contiguous slots
4) If scale-up still blocked, fallback: manual placement override for highest-priority large-gangs to us-west1a.

maria: I can run step 3 now. command I'm going to run:
```
kubectl get pods -n burst | grep worker | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -r -n1 kubectl delete pod -n burst --grace-period=0 --force
```

devon: Wait before deleting — use evict API to respect PDBs: `kubectl evict` not delete. Also tag the jobs we evict so we can restore quickly.

maria: good call. i'll use evict + label. doing it. @oncall FYI.

infra-bot: Eviction batch started: 120 pods targeted, 98 evicted so far, 22 deferred by PDBs.

leo: After evictions, check `kubectl describe node` on candidate nodes to ensure they have 8 free GPUs contiguous. Also look at nvlink locality if job needs multi-GPU on same host.

maria: evictions finished. freed ~40 GPUs total, but still fragmented across hosts. pulled one large job onto us-west1b — it scheduled but reported OOM on init (insufficient contiguous memory). Rolling back and moving next ones to us-west1a.

devon: Suggest we add a scheduler tweak: temporarily relax podAntiAffinity hard rule for this class of jobs (add toleration or lower topologySpread constraints) so we can place across more nodes. We'll revert after backlog clears.

anya: Policy/approval check: relaxing anti-affinity may compromise isolation for some customers. Only do for non-prod / internal queues. Need @sam signoff for cost vs risk.

sam: OK for burst-workers and internal benches. For customer workloads we must keep constraints. Proceed with dev/non-prod relax. :+1:

maria: Actioned — label `queue=internal-burst` now has relaxed affinity. Moved 12 pending large-gang jobs to us-west1a. All green so far.

leo: Follow-ups:
- add placement defragmenter job to consolidate tiny pods overnight (binpack by GPU count)
- reduce taint footprint: only reserve minimal dedicated nodes instead of broad reserved=true on entire warmpool
- autoscaler: expose fragmentation metric and set policy to prefer new full-node allocations over partial slots.

devon: I'll open a short RFC for the defragmenter + autoscaler frag metric.

maria: Current status: 12 moved successfully, 8 remain pending (low priority), warmpool.min bumped +4 pending provisioning. Will update if warmpool nodes come up or we need full region fallback. :shipit:
